subject: European hosting & SOC 2: audit window, bridge letter & transfer legal basis
messages:
From: Sophie Levesque <sophie.levesque@eurofintrust.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: SOC 2, hosting mapping and transfer legal basis for EU customers

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this — I'm the security lead supporting EuroFinTrust's procurement/legal review. We have a few specific questions to close our Vendor Risk Assessment around regional processing and cross-border transfers:

- Please attach your latest SOC 2 Type II report and confirm the audit coverage window (start/end dates).
- Do you provide a bridge letter if an audit window doesn't align with our procurement timeline? If so, what's the typical scope and turnaround?
- For the hosted offering, can you provide a mapping of which control plane components and data plane components are physically located in the EU vs the US? We need to understand whether customer content can be restricted to EEA regions.
- What is the legal basis used for transfers from the EEA (SCCs, adequacy decision, other)? Do you include SCCs in your DPA?
- Can you share your current subprocessors list and whether any subprocessors have access to unencrypted customer content?

I've attached our standard questionnaire (EuroFinTrust_Security_Request.xlsx) — it's not exhaustive but highlights what our compliance team needs for sign-off.

Would appreciate a short response by end of week; if it's easier, we can slot a 30-minute call next week with our DPO to walk through the items.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Levesque
Head of Security Assurance
EuroFinTrust

Subject: Re: SOC 2, hosting mapping and transfer legal basis for EU customers

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. I'm copying Markus (infrastructure security) and Vanessa (privacy/commercial) so we can cover both technical and contractual items. Quick responses below and I've attached our most recent artifacts.

1) SOC 2 Type II report
- Attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (covers period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31).
- We understand procurement teams often request a bridge letter when the audit window doesn't overlap with the approval window; we can provide a bridge letter scoped to the controls tested in the 2025 Type II report. Typical turnaround for a draft bridge letter is 3 business days.

2) Hosting & regional mapping (high level)
- Data plane (customer content) can be pinned to EU regions for both Hosted API and Dedicated deployments. EU region processing means inference and storage are performed on EU-based infrastructure.
- Control plane (metadata/orchestration) is currently operated from our global control plane; certain control plane telemetry routes via the US. We do not store customer content in the US when customer selects EU region.

3) Transfer legal basis
- We operate under standard EU SCCs embedded in our DPA and include SCC annex by reference. We can provide a redlineable DPA with SCCs and a subprocessors addendum.

4) Subprocessors and encryption
- Current subprocessor register link (public copy) provided below. No subprocessors have access to unencrypted customer content when customer enables BYOK or uses our EU KMS region option.

Next steps: attaching the SOC 2 report and a draft bridge letter for review. Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday or Friday next week? If helpful, we can include our DPO/Privacy counsel.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SOC 2, hosting mapping and transfer legal basis for EU customers

Hi Sophie — Markus here from Infra Security, thanks for the thoughtful questions. Short technical clarifications below (happy to expand on the call):

- Customer content: when a customer chooses an EU region, inference and persistent storage (buckets, DBs for model responses/kvs where configured) are provisioned in EU data centers only. We do not persist raw customer prompts in US datastores for EU-region customers.
- Control plane telemetry: control plane metadata (orchestration, routing decisions, job lifecycle events) may emit non-content telemetry to services that are global; those telemetry streams do not contain raw customer content by design. We treat prompt/response content as data plane.
- EEA-only requirement: our Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is the recommended option when a customer requires a fully EEA-contained control plane. We also offer an EU-dedicated control plane add-on for large enterprise customers as a contractual option — delivery timeline is typically 8-12 weeks for onboarding and validation.
- KMS/BYOK: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) hosted in EU KMS providers. When BYOK is enabled and configured in EU, Redwood holds no plaintext access to content keys; all decryption occurs within customer-controlled KMS boundaries.
- Subprocessors: full register is available via the link below, and subprocessors that handle encrypted files do so under strict contractual terms.

If you'd like, we can prepare a concise one-page mapping (Control Plane vs Data Plane) showing exactly which components are EU-hosted for your procurement team.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure Security
markus_klein@redwood.com
